articles.title: Chrome will now show a warning before you visit ‘suspicious’ sites
articles.author: Jess Weatherbed
articles.content:
Google is launching a new browser safety feature for Chrome that aims to keep you better informed about how malicious a website might be before you open it. The new suspicious site warnings, available when Chrome’s Enhanced Protection is on, build on a similar two-stage system introduced for Chrome file downloads in 2024, which provides visually different notifications for blocked files based on whether they’re determined to be “suspicious” or “dangerous.”
Chrome will now show a warning before you visit ‘suspicious’ sites
The new two-stage browser warning makes it easier to distinguish between shifty and dangerous URLs.
For the Chrome site warnings, the feature will flag a website as suspicious if it detects that it has similar qualities to other sites associated with phishing, malware, and scams. Google describes this warning as having a “lower confidence verdict” with possible risk of user harm — meaning there’s a chance it could be incorrectly flagged, but you should only proceed to the site if you’re 100 percent confident that it’s safe to do so. The warnings on “dangerous” website have a higher confidence verdict and “high risk of user harm,” however, and should be avoided entirely.
It’s easy to distinguish between these warnings at a glance. The notifications for suspicious websites will appear as a pop-up window on both desktop and mobile, with the webpage visible but darkened underneath, and an option to “Mark as safe” if the site was flagged mistakenly. The already familiar notification for dangerous sites is much harder to ignore: the warning message takes up almost the entire screen and the website will be replaced with a solid red background.
Google also improved Gemini-powered scam detection for Enhanced Protection users, alongside introducing the browser warning redesign.
Update, October 20th: Clarified that the suspicious site warnings appear when Enhanced Protection mode is on.
articles.summary:
Google is rolling out a new two-stage warning system for Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode that alerts users to potentially suspicious websites before they navigate to the page.

### Key Points
- The feature distinguishes between "suspicious" sites with lower-confidence risk and "dangerous" sites with high-confidence threats.
- Suspicious site warnings appear as pop-ups, while dangerous site alerts occupy the full screen with a red background.
- Users can manually override suspicious site warnings by selecting a "Mark as safe" option if they believe the flag is incorrect.
- This update builds upon the two-stage file download security system Google introduced earlier in 2024.
- Google has simultaneously integrated improved Gemini-powered scam detection for users enrolled in Enhanced Protection.

### Why it Matters
This update provides users with more granular security data, allowing for better-informed browsing decisions when encountering potentially malicious URLs. By differentiating between varying levels of risk, Google aims to reduce accidental exposure to phishing and malware while minimizing user frustration from false positives.

articles.title: As Midterms Approach, Top American Fears Include AI Interference in the Political Process
articles.author: Blake Stimac
articles.content:
Are you more fearful of AI stealing jobs, hurting the economy and disrupting the political process than you are of someone you love dying? A lot of people are, according to Chapman University’s 12th annual survey on American fears for 2026.
This year’s survey by the private research university in California was different. For the first time, researchers began asking Americans about their thoughts and fears about artificial intelligence, and those AI-related fears made the top 10 twice, as well as popping up throughout the list.
These were the top fears in the minds of the American people for 2026.
More from CNET
| Fear | % of very afraid or afraid | Rank in 2025 | 
|---|---|---|
| Corrupt government officials | 61.1% | 1 | 
| US becoming involved in another world war | 58% | 6 | 
| AI harming the political process | 51.9% | New entry | 
| People I love becoming seriously ill | 51.8% | 2 | 
| People I love dying | 50.6% | 5 | 
| Economic/financial collapse | 50.6% | 3 | 
| AI hurting the economy | 49.7% | New entry | 
| Government tracking of personal data | 48.9% | 10 | 
| Biological warfare | 48.2% | 12 | 
| Terrorist attack | 47.3% | 15 | 
The most central fear for Americans has remained unchanged since last year: corrupt government officials, at a staggering 61.1%. Other common and expected fears, like the US becoming involved in another world war, remain on the list, but it now sits in the No. 2 spot instead of 2025’s No. 6 slot.
Possibly the most common fears that any human could have — someone you love becoming seriously ill or dying — also remained prominent in the top 10 list.
The addition of AI makes a lot of sense in the world that we live in today, however. In the top 10 list, AI-related fears surround the technology harming both the election process (ranked third) and the economy (ranked seventh). With midterm elections right around the corner, it’s not at all surprising to see AI pop up here.
The team at Chapman commissioned NORC at the University of Chicago to survey 1,221 adults online this past April.
The study doesn’t paint AI as all bad, though. It also states that there is hope about the technology, according to Seth Benzell, assistant professor of business and economics at Chapman.
“When you frame it as AI or robots that are going to allow you to build something that you weren’t able to do before … those get people a lot more excited,” Benzell said.
AI cropped up a few more times on the list, however, including AI hurting the environment (at 43.2%), AI harming personal relationships (42%), AI replacing people in the workforce (also 42%), reporting to an AI manager at work (19.1%), having your work evaluated by AI (19.3%) and working with AI-enabled technologies (17.2%).
Other fears of technology also made the list: government tracking of personal data (48.9%), cyberterrorism (45.7%), government use of drones within the US (34.2%), technology that I don’t understand (23.5%) and technological change at work (12.6%).
Other, hardly dismissible fears that have been on people’s minds for a long time remain on the list: economic collapse, biological warfare and terrorist attacks are all incredibly valid.
articles.summary:
Chapman University’s 12th annual survey reveals that Americans now rank artificial intelligence’s impact on politics and the economy among their top ten most significant national fears for 2026.

### Key Points
- Corrupt government officials remain the top American fear, cited by 61.1% of the 1,221 adults surveyed by NORC.
- Concerns regarding the U.S. entering another world war rose to the second position, affecting 58% of respondents.
- AI harming the political process debuted at number three, while AI hurting the economy entered the list at number seven.
- Personal fears, including the illness or death of loved ones, continue to rank within the top five concerns for the public.
- The survey, conducted in April, highlights that 42% of Americans fear AI will replace human workers.

### Why it Matters
The inclusion of artificial intelligence in the top ten list reflects growing public anxiety regarding the rapid integration of new technology into daily life and governance. This shift suggests that policymakers and businesses must address these societal concerns to maintain public trust as AI tools become more prevalent in the workforce and political landscape.

articles.title: Musk opens the door to a SpaceX-Tesla merger as shareholders weigh a deal
articles.author: Alex PIGMAN
articles.content:
Elon Musk said Tuesday he would back a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, as his rocket and AI company reported its first quarterly profit since going public, driven by deals to rent out computing power to AI firms.
Asked about a possible tie-up on a call with analysts, Musk said he felt he was "tap dancing through a minefield," but that a combination would be "a good idea."
Shares in SpaceX shot up nearly five percent in after-hours trading following the comments.
Musk said special committees of independent directors at both SpaceX and Tesla have been set up to study the idea at the request of shareholders.
He added that he could not take part in their talks because he has a conflict of interest.
Musk is chief executive of both companies, and also serves as chairman and chief technology officer of SpaceX.
He owned 48.4 percent of SpaceX as of June 30, according to a regulatory filing, and controls more than 82 percent of its voting power through super-voting shares.
He holds about 20 percent of Tesla.
The committees have not agreed on the terms of any deal and there is no guarantee they will, Musk said, cautioning that it would be overstating it to treat a merger as a certainty.
Any deal would need the backing of a majority of all Tesla shares, not just those cast in a vote, which Musk called "quite a high hurdle."
He said the two companies could gain from working together on AI software, chip design, robotics and space-based computing.
His remarks came after SpaceX posted net income of $4.4 billion for the July-September period, compared with a loss of $1.1 billion a year earlier.
Revenue jumped 161 percent to $14.6 billion. The quarterly results follow a bumpy start on Wall Street.
SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq on June 12 after an IPO priced at $135 a share that raised about $85.7 billion.
Its first earnings report as a listed company showed second-quarter revenue of $7.8 billion and a net loss of $541 million.
The AI division, which SpaceX now calls "Super Intelligence," drove the turnaround. Super Intelligence is US President Donald Trump's preferred term for AI.
The unit's revenue rose more than nine times from a year earlier to $7.6 billion, overtaking the Starlink satellite internet business as the company's largest source of sales.
- Cloud computing -
SpaceX credited new cloud services agreements, wider adoption of its Grok chatbot and its acquisition of Cursor, an artificial intelligence coding startup.
SpaceX's cloud customers include Anthropic, which agreed in May to pay nearly $45 billion over three years for computing power at SpaceX's Colossus data centers.
articles.summary:
Elon Musk has confirmed that independent committees are evaluating a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla following the rocket company's first profitable quarter as a public entity.

### Key Points
- SpaceX reported a $4.4 billion net profit for the third quarter, driven by $7.6 billion in revenue from its "Super Intelligence" AI division.
- The company's total quarterly revenue reached $14.6 billion, a 161 percent increase compared to the previous year.
- SpaceX shares rose nearly five percent in after-hours trading following Musk's comments regarding the potential corporate combination.
- Independent directors at both companies are currently studying the merger proposal, though no formal terms have been established.
- Anthropic remains a major client, having committed $45 billion over three years for computing power at SpaceX’s Colossus data centers.

### Why it Matters
A merger between these two industry giants would create a massive conglomerate focused on AI, robotics, and space-based computing. Investors face significant uncertainty, however, as the deal requires approval from a majority of all Tesla shareholders and must navigate complex conflicts of interest.

articles.title: Amazon is buying billions in Nvidia AI systems it can't yet turn on
articles.author: Eugene Kim
articles.content:
Amazon is racing to secure AI hardware earlier than before, even as data center power shortages leave some GPU systems waiting in warehouses.
Under a new Early Rack Receipt process, AWS expected to receive roughly $5 billion in Nvidia's GB300 server racks at US facilities before final deployment, according to August internal emails reviewed by Business Insider. The company projected roughly $3 billion more in GB300 racks each month "for the foreseeable future," one of the emails said.
Some AWS sites had room for more racks but not enough available power to turn them on, people familiar with the effort said, leaving finished equipment to be staged at intermediary warehouses until the facilities were ready.
At least one AWS team did not have "a clear forecasted path" for getting the incoming racks into data centers at the time, according to one of the emails.
Dark GPUs
A lack of new electricity capacity is one of several bottlenecks slowing the buildout of some AI data centers. This has led to a phenomenon known as dark GPUs, where AI chips and servers are purchased but can sit idle due to power supply issues or other challenges. (Dark GPUs can also refer to system design flaws that mean this gear isn't fully used after being plugged in).
This is partly why financial pressure is mounting on big data center projects. Money must be spent upfront to secure supplies of Nvidia GPUs and other valuable AI components. But if some data centers aren't ready to run, those early investments can tie up huge amounts of cash. Debt financing can fill in the gaps, but the market has become less willing to lend against some of these projects lately.
Trade-off
Amazon's early-rack program is one piece of the cloud leader's broader AI buildout, which is putting new pressure on its cash flow, as Business Insider exclusively reported this week. Amazon expects roughly $220 billion in capital expenditures this year — more than any Big Tech peer. Its free-cash-flow turned negative last quarter for the first time since 2023, and could stay negative for a while.
For AWS, the trade-off is securing scarce GPU racks before competitors do, even if some data centers are not yet ready to turn them on. But taking ownership earlier can tie up billions in equipment before it starts generating cloud revenue.
Previously, AWS took ownership of a finished rack only upon delivery to a data center, according to internal documents. Under the new approach, it can pay for and record certain racks earlier in the supply chain.
An Amazon spokesperson said the company routinely stages finished hardware near deployment sites so it can install it once capacity becomes available, calling the practice "best business practice." The spokesperson added that Amazon has long-established systems for tracking infrastructure assets and disputed that the broader company lacked a path for getting racks into data centers.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy previously said the company has a "clear line of sight" to strong returns from its AI investments, calling the technology a "once in a lifetime opportunity."
"We've been through this cycle with the first big AWS growth wave, and liked the results," Jassy wrote in Amazon's annual shareholder letter. "We expect to feel similarly about this next wave."

articles.summary:
Amazon is accelerating its acquisition of Nvidia GB300 server racks to secure AI hardware, despite power shortages at data centers causing equipment to sit idle in warehouses.

### Key Points
- Amazon has implemented an Early Rack Receipt process to take ownership of Nvidia hardware earlier in the supply chain.
- Internal emails indicate AWS planned to receive $5 billion in GB300 racks initially, followed by $3 billion in monthly shipments.
- Power capacity constraints at various data centers have forced the company to stage finished server equipment in intermediary warehouses.
- Amazon projects approximately $220 billion in capital expenditures for the year, the highest among major technology companies.
- The company’s free cash flow turned negative last quarter as it prioritizes securing scarce AI components over immediate deployment.

### Why it Matters
This strategy highlights the intense competition among cloud providers to secure limited AI hardware, even at the risk of tying up billions in capital. While the move ensures supply, it creates significant financial pressure and operational challenges as companies struggle to align hardware delivery with available data center power.

articles.title: Apple is looking for a cellular modem engineer to help shape its transition to 6G
articles.author: Marcus Mendes
articles.content:
Apple is looking for an experienced cellular modem systems engineer to help develop its next generation of cellular modems as the company transitions toward 6G. Here are the details.
‘A rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication’
As spotted by MacRumors, Apple listed a new job opening yesterday for a 6G Cellular Modem Systems Engineer, with a base salary range of $175,000 to $308,500 per year, plus stock awards and other benefits.
From the job listing:
We’re looking for a Cellular Modem Systems Engineer to join our cellular systems engineering team as we define and build the next generation of cellular technology. This is a rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication at a company that ships at global scale as we transition towards 6G. In this role, you’ll bring an end-to-end view of wireless systems — spanning 3GPP standards, feature definition and planning, design, hardware and software architecture and partitioning — to deliver leading-edge performance and power optimizations and features that directly improve the user experience across Apple products. If you thrive at the intersection of deep technical theory and hands-on bring-up — and you’re excited about pushing beyond 5G into the 6G era — we want to hear from you.
Apple says the candidate’s responsibilities will include defining features and requirements for next-generation cellular modems, designing algorithms to improve performance and power efficiency, and working with hardware and software teams to bring those technologies to market.
The candidate should have a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field, along with at least 10 years of industry experience working with cellular technologies.
Apple also requires a strong understanding of cellular communication standards and proficiency in MATLAB, C/C++, or Python.
Interestingly, Apple also lists experience with generative AI and LLM-based tools “to accelerate engineering workflows” as a minimum qualification. Ideally, the candidate should also have a track record of published research or patents in wireless communications, among other preferred qualifications.
For context, 6G is still years away and in the early stages of development, as companies and industry organizations work to define what it will look like.
Top comment by Tudor
I really wonder why we never push existing technology to its limits before moving on to something that’s much crazier and that we will never achieve either.
I don’t recall 5G in practice being anywhere near 20Gbps. Not even 5Gbps. Heck, in most cases, it’s not even 2Gbps. And now we’re done with it and moving to 6G already?
The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) has outlined potential peak speeds of up to 200 Gbps, compared to 5G’s theoretical maximum of 20 Gbps, along with research targets for latency as low as 0.1 milliseconds.
AI is also expected to play a much bigger role in 6G, helping networks automatically adjust to changing conditions, optimize signal quality, manage traffic, and reduce power consumption.
The first official 6G technical specifications are expected to be finalized in late 2028, with commercial networks and compatible devices anticipated around 2030.
You can find more details about the position in Apple’s full job listing here.
articles.summary:
Apple has posted a job listing for a 6G Cellular Modem Systems Engineer to lead the development of next-generation wireless technology and improve future hardware performance.

### Key Points
- The position offers an annual base salary between $175,000 and $308,500, plus additional stock awards and benefits.
- Candidates must possess at least 10 years of industry experience and proficiency in programming languages like C/C++, Python, or MATLAB.
- Apple requires expertise in generative AI and LLM-based tools to help accelerate internal engineering workflows and system design.
- The role involves defining 6G standards, hardware architecture, and power optimization strategies for future Apple product integration.
- Industry standards for 6G aim for peak speeds of 200 Gbps and latency as low as 0.1 milliseconds.
- Commercial 6G networks and compatible consumer devices are not expected to reach the market until approximately 2030.

### Why it Matters
This recruitment effort signals Apple's long-term strategy to reduce reliance on third-party modem suppliers by building proprietary wireless technology. By integrating generative AI into the development process, the company aims to accelerate the complex transition from 5G to 6G standards.

articles.title: GitHub package firewall
articles.author: Allison
articles.content:
Editor’s note (October 21, 2026): Rewrote the changelog for clarity and added imagery.
There’s been a recent flood of malware attacks that exploit systems at package installation time. Agents and CI runners are particularly vulnerable to these attacks because they install dependencies to accomplish a task or complete a build without a human in the loop. To stem this tide, GitHub is introducing a new package firewall, which sits between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories. The firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity, acting as an install-time policy gate. The package firewall is available today in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
First, administrators set policy controls for their enterprise. The controls available today include a configurable cooldown period, checking the GitHub Advisory Database for malware or vulnerability advisories, and supply-chain checks like attestation downgrades.
Then, endpoints like coding agents and CI/CD hosts use the firewall for their requests instead of pointing directly at the upstream package registries. Metadata requests for package lists as well as the actual package downloads flow through the firewall, which evaluates them against the policy. If a package is blocked erroneously, the user can request an exception with a workflow similar to other GitHub Advanced Security features.
The package firewall is available in public preview as we scale up the infrastructure behind it and continue to add features based on customer demand. It is available to GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. The service is free while in the preview period. When it reaches general availability, it will be charged based on metered usage, similar to Actions billing.
Currently the package firewall only supports npm packages.
For detailed setup instructions, see Protecting endpoints with package firewall. Join the discussion in GitHub Community.
articles.summary:
GitHub has launched a new package firewall in public preview to protect enterprise CI runners and coding agents from malicious software during the automated dependency installation process.

### Key Points
- The firewall acts as a policy gate, inspecting metadata and package downloads for malicious activity before they reach internal systems.
- Administrators can configure security controls, including cooldown periods, GitHub Advisory Database checks, and supply-chain attestation verification.
- The service is currently available to all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers at no cost during the public preview period.
- Initial support is limited exclusively to npm packages, with plans to scale infrastructure and features based on user demand.
- Blocked packages can be appealed through an exception request workflow similar to existing GitHub Advanced Security features.

### Why it Matters
This security layer addresses critical vulnerabilities in automated build environments where human oversight is often absent during dependency installation. By centralizing policy enforcement, organizations can significantly reduce the risk of supply-chain attacks infiltrating their development pipelines.

articles.title: Your Windows laptop has crucial security settings that you're probably ignoring
articles.author: Tanveer Singh
articles.content:
Unlike your desktop, your laptop is exposed to several threat vectors simply because it leaves the safety of your home, giving attackers many more ways to steal it or compromise your data. That's not to say that you shouldn't enable basic security settings on your desktop, but they become way more critical on your Windows laptop.
While some security settings are enabled by default on a new Windows 11 installation, you have to manually opt in to others. By enabling them, you effectively make it harder for attackers to threaten or steal your data even if they gain control of your machine. They'll also help if someone intends to mess with your data or settings when your laptop is unattended.
Controlled folder access
Prevent unauthorized data encryption and deletion
I'm assuming your laptop doubles up as your work machine and possibly stores some of your financial information, too. Even if it doesn't leave the house, it can still get caught up in a ransomware attack. Attackers routinely use unassuming entry points like phishing emails, malicious websites, and pirated media to inject ransomware into thousands of machines. Your unprotected folders can be held for ransom before you know what happened.
Although Windows Security protects against ransomware and other types of security attacks, enabling Controlled folder access (CFA) can provide your data with an additional layer of protection. Even if a new ransomware strain bypasses the default security controls, CFA will prevent it from modifying your files, since it will not have the necessary permissions. CFA will block the attacks and notify you of the same.
It also protects critical boot sectors from boot-level ransomware, so attackers can't lock you out of the entire OS. You can toggle CFA on by navigating to Settings > Privacy & security > Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage ransomware protection, or simply searching for it in the search bar. By default, CFA protects folders like Documents, Pictures, Music, and Videos, but you can add any other folder you want to protect.
Dynamic lock
Automatically lock your device when you walk away
If you aren't in the habit of manually locking your laptop in a library or café when walking away for a glass of water or a bio break, anyone can gain access to your unattended device. It doesn't have to be a determined attacker after your sensitive data. It could simply be a prying stranger or even a friend intent on causing mischief. Your screen lock settings might take too long to lock your laptop, so enabling Dynamic lock can provide a backup layer of protection.
Enabling it requires pairing your laptop with your smartphone, so that Windows can detect when you've left your device unattended. It monitors the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) of your phone's Bluetooth connection, waiting for it to drop below a certain threshold. It waits for about 30 to 60 seconds before locking your laptop, preventing unauthorized access. You can find Dynamic lock at Settings > Account > Sign-in options > Dynamic lock.
Although the physical environment around the laptop can influence the distance needed to trigger the lock, this is still a useful setting to enable. Note that someone can still access your device within the 30-to-60-second grace period.
Device encryption
Hide your data from prying eyes
Most new Windows laptops have device encryption enabled by default, but you may have disabled BitLocker on your laptop for fear of a performance penalty. However, the benefits of BitLocker easily outweigh any negligible performance impact it might have on a modern laptop. Features like CFA can protect your data from unauthorized modification, but Full Disk Encryption (FDE) protects your entire drive.
Without the decryption key, nobody can access the data on your drive. If an attacker removes your hard drive or SSD from the laptop and plugs it into another computer, they can't make sense of the data without the BitLocker Recovery key. You can enable device encryption at Settings > Privacy & security > Device encryption.
Attackers can obviously erase a stolen drive or laptop and sell it to make some cash, but FDE ensures your data remains safe from unauthorized access.
Tamper Protection
Who will guard the guards?
Each of the settings above involves setting up an additional security layer to protect your data, but what if someone disables the said security controls themselves? Malware is sophisticated enough to take control of your laptop by slowly dismantling your security settings. All of your carefully curated security features will do nothing if malware manages to disable them.
This is why enabling Tamper Protection is essential, not just on laptops but even on desktops. This feature stops apps and processes from making any changes to your machine's security infrastructure. While you, as an administrator, can still tweak your security settings, any app pr process is blocked. You can toggle Tamper Protection on at Settings > Privacy & security > Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings (under Virus & threat protection settings).
Enable these security settings on a new Windows laptop
Microsoft's built-in security settings have gotten fairly robust over time, so much so that many users don't use third-party protection at all. When you're setting up a new laptop, many of these settings are pre-enabled, but you still need to turn others on. These settings will protect your laptop both inside and outside your house by preventing attackers from gaining unauthorized access or disabling the security features themselves.
articles.summary:
Windows 11 users can significantly enhance their laptop security by manually enabling key features like Controlled folder access, Dynamic lock, device encryption, and Tamper Protection to prevent unauthorized access.

### Key Points
- Controlled folder access prevents ransomware from modifying or deleting files in protected directories like Documents and Pictures.
- Dynamic lock automatically secures your device by monitoring the Bluetooth signal strength of a paired smartphone when you walk away.
- BitLocker device encryption protects data on your hard drive or SSD, ensuring information remains unreadable if the hardware is stolen.
- Tamper Protection prevents malicious apps and processes from disabling your Windows Security settings or security infrastructure.
- These settings are accessible through the Windows Settings menu under Privacy & security or the Virus & threat protection dashboard.

### Why it Matters
Enabling these built-in Windows features provides a critical layer of defense for mobile devices that are frequently exposed to public networks and physical theft. By hardening these settings, users can effectively mitigate the risk of data breaches and ransomware attacks without needing third-party security software.

articles.title: 7 Best Virtualization Platforms for Hybrid Cloud Environments
articles.author: Ryan Kh
articles.content:
Pick the wrong virtualization platform and your IT team eats years of rework. Since Broadcom’s acquisition of VMware, pricing disruption has pushed thousands of enterprises to reassess what actually runs under their workloads. The market for virtualization platforms built for hybrid cloud environments has shifted hard. What follows is a look at seven platforms worth serious evaluation, ranked by overall fit for enterprise hybrid cloud deployments.
Platform selection at a glance
- Sangfor aSV and Nutanix package compute with other infrastructure services. Compare what the platform license includes, especially networking and storage.
- VMware offers a deep ecosystem, while Proxmox gives teams an open-source option with more hands-on configuration.
- Red Hat, Hyper-V, and Oracle fit different starting conditions: container modernization, Microsoft/Azure commitments, and Oracle-heavy applications.
- Hypervisors still connect on-premises and public-cloud operations, as discussed in WindowsForum’s virtualization coverage. Your existing estate affects the migration work behind each choice.
Why Virtualization Matters in Hybrid Cloud
A hypervisor is the layer that makes hybrid cloud work. It abstracts compute resources so workloads can move between on-premises servers and public cloud infrastructure without being rebuilt for each environment. Strip away a capable virtualization layer, and “hybrid cloud” is mostly a marketing term.
The platforms here differ on dimensions that actually matter. Is networking and storage bundled or sold separately? How does migration tooling handle an existing VMware estate? Does the hypervisor run on broad commodity hardware or a narrow certified list? What level of vendor support ships with the license? Pricing transparency varies wildly too. Some vendors publish rates openly; others require a quote call before IT can even run a cost comparison. For teams building or rearchitecting a hybrid cloud stack, those differences add up fast.
What it does: Sangfor aSV is a type-1, KVM-based bare-metal hypervisor from Sangfor Technologies. It installs directly on x86 servers from Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and others, and serves as the compute virtualization layer inside Sangfor’s Hyper-Converged Infrastructure and Cloud Platform stacks. It’s positioned as an enterprise VMware vSphere alternative for mid-market and large organizations reassessing their virtualization spend after Broadcom’s pricing changes.
Where it shines: The clearest structural advantage is bundling. VMware prices NSX (networking) and vSAN (storage) as separate add-ons; aSV folds networking, storage, and security – WAF, IPS, and intelligent micro-segmentation through aSEC – into the same license. Migration tooling is purpose-built: the platform ships over 230 commands equivalent to PowerCLI, so existing VMware automation scripts carry over rather than getting rewritten from scratch. Live migration stays under 3 seconds of measured performance impact, and Proactive HA 2.0 flags likely node failures before they cause outages rather than responding after. Sangfor cites more than 12,000 completed VMware migrations and 28,000+ cloud customers globally.
On G2, Sangfor Cloud Platform holds a 4.7 out of 5 rating across 94 reviews, with a Leader badge in Server Virtualization for Summer 2026. Gartner Peer Insights shows a 4.9 overall rating from verified enterprise reviewers, with 100% Willingness to Recommend across 23 enterprise reviews. Sangfor named it a Representative Vendor in the 2025 Gartner Market Guide for Server Virtualization Platforms.
2. VMware
What it does: VMware, now a Broadcom subsidiary, offers the VMware Cloud Foundation stack, vSphere Foundation, and a broad set of advanced services covering disaster recovery, container operations, private AI infrastructure, edge orchestration, and load balancing. With 38,300 employees as of 2023 and $13.4 billion in revenue, it’s the largest pure-play virtualization vendor by a wide margin. VMware Cloud Foundation won a 2025 Tech CUBEd Award for most advanced cloud infrastructure solution.
Where it shines: Ecosystem depth. VMware’s published case studies cover a range of industries, and the community of trained vSphere admins, third-party integrations, and partner tooling is larger than any other vendor on this list. Grinnell Mutual saved $1 million in infrastructure costs using VMware Cloud Foundation; GCI deployed VMware Cloud Foundation alongside Tanzu Data Services for a full-stack hybrid cloud build. Broadcom’s licensing restructuring pushed SMB pricing up sharply – Sangfor’s own blog cites increases of up to tenfold in some cases. Teams renewing VMware contracts now should model the full cost of VMware Cloud Foundation before comparing, since advanced networking and storage capabilities are bundled at a higher price tier.
3. Nutanix
What it does: Nutanix sells the Nutanix Cloud Platform, which packages AOS storage, AHV virtualization, Nutanix Flow networking, Kubernetes management, database-as-a-service, and enterprise AI tooling into a single HCI platform. Founded in 2009 and publicly traded on NASDAQ (NTNX), Nutanix employs around 7,800 people and targets organizations running hybrid and multicloud workloads that need a single management plane across environments.
A hybrid cloud platform runs and manages workloads across more than one kind of environment: public cloud regions, your own data centers, bare metal servers, and increasingly neoclouds, the GPU-focused providers that supply AI capacity.
Noah Grinstein in 9 Best Hybrid Cloud Platforms in 2026 — Control Plane
Where it shines: Analyst positioning is strong. Nutanix is named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Server Virtualization Platforms with the highest Execution score, and a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Distributed Hybrid Infrastructure. The platform also holds a Challenger position in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Container Management. AHV is a capable no-license-cost hypervisor included with the Nutanix stack, attractive for organizations standardizing on Nutanix’s full platform rather than paying separately for compute virtualization. Nutanix requires a narrower vendor-certified hardware list compared to platforms that support broad commodity x86 hardware. Teams with existing server infrastructure outside that list should verify compatibility before committing.
4. Proxmox
What it does: Proxmox Virtual Environment, from Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH in Vienna, Austria, is an open-source virtualization platform combining KVM-based virtualization and container-based virtualization in a single interface. The company also offers Proxmox Backup Server, Proxmox Mail Gateway, and Proxmox Datacenter Manager. Founded in 2005, Proxmox has 68 employees and manages more than 1.5 million hosts globally across partnerships with over 1,000 resellers in 142 countries.
Where it shines: Cost. The full feature set is available without a commercial subscription, which makes Proxmox the natural first look for budget-constrained teams and organizations that want open-source infrastructure they can self-manage. Customers include the European Space Agency, YouTube, Huawei Technologies, and Northrop Grumman. The vendor claims approximately 95% of VMware deployments can migrate to Proxmox VE without issue, and partnerships with NVIDIA and Veeam extend what it can connect to. Proxmox requires considerably more manual configuration than appliance-style platforms. Storage and networking are assembled separately, and high availability and disaster recovery demand hands-on setup. Commercial support comes through remote ticketing only.
5. Red Hat
What it does: Red Hat, a subsidiary of IBM since 2019, delivers Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), OpenShift Container Platform, Ansible Automation Platform, and Red Hat AI. Its virtualization story runs through OpenShift Virtualization, which lets teams run traditional VM workloads alongside containerized applications on a Kubernetes-native platform. Red Hat has 19,000 employees and supports more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies across automotive, financial services, healthcare, public sector, and telecommunications.
Where it shines: Red Hat’s strength is with organizations modernizing toward containers and cloud-native application platforms. Red Hat was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud-Native Application Platforms for a third consecutive year, and holds a fourth consecutive Leaders Quadrant position in a separate Gartner Magic Quadrant. For teams already running Ansible for automation, the operational continuity is real – the tooling integrates directly without additional bridging work. OpenShift Virtualization is a strong fit for container-first shops but may carry more overhead than a purpose-built hypervisor for teams whose primary workload is traditional VM management. That tradeoff is worth sweating before you commit.
What it does: Hyper-V is Microsoft’s native type-1 hypervisor for x86-64 systems, released in June 2008 and built into Windows Server. It runs directly on physical hardware with near-native performance, supports Windows, Linux, and FreeBSD guest operating systems, and is the hypervisor underpinning Azure Stack for on-premises hybrid cloud scenarios. Microsoft was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in Redmond, Washington. WindowsForum’s 2026 virtualization overview describes the continuing role of hypervisors in isolating workloads and connecting on-premises and public-cloud environments.
Where it shines: Windows-heavy environments. Organizations already running Windows Server licensing get Hyper-V included, keeping acquisition costs low. The Azure integration story is coherent too – organizations standardizing on Azure as their public cloud extension benefit from Hyper-V’s tight alignment with Azure Site Recovery, Azure Migrate, and Azure Arc. Server consolidation and performance are well-documented use cases. Hyper-V’s management tooling and ecosystem are tightly coupled to the Microsoft stack. Teams running mixed operating environments or planning workloads outside the Azure orbit may find those advantages less compelling than they look on paper.
7. Oracle
What it does: Oracle Corporation, founded in 1977 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, delivers Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) alongside its flagship Oracle Database and a broad suite of Oracle Cloud Applications. OCI covers IaaS and SaaS, including Oracle Fusion ERP, EPM, SCM, HCM, NetSuite, and Oracle Health. Oracle employs approximately 141,000 people and generated $67.36 billion in revenue in 2026.
Where it shines: Database-heavy and Oracle-application-centric organizations. OCI is architected to run Oracle Database workloads at performance levels that competing clouds have historically struggled to match for Oracle-native applications. For enterprises whose hybrid cloud design centers on Oracle ERP or large Oracle Database deployments, OCI’s infrastructure is purpose-aligned in a way generic IaaS alternatives aren’t. Oracle’s scale – $261.76 billion in total assets – signals long-term platform commitment. Oracle’s ecosystem advantages narrow considerably for organizations that don’t rely heavily on Oracle applications or databases. Teams with a mixed application portfolio may find OCI’s benefits less differentiated compared to broader multi-cloud hypervisors.
Comparing Platform Scope and Operational Fit
Compare these seven options by what they package and the environment your team already operates. Sangfor and Nutanix emphasize integrated stacks; Proxmox leaves more assembly to administrators. Red Hat, Hyper-V, and Oracle align with specific application or cloud commitments, while VMware offers an established ecosystem with changed licensing economics.
The shortlist includes individual hypervisors, broader HCI platforms, and OCI’s cloud services. Those scopes affect the comparison: Oracle’s application fit answers a different question from Proxmox’s hypervisor licensing. VMware also offers multiple packages, including vSphere Foundation, which its product page describes as an enterprise-class hyperconverged infrastructure workload platform.
| Platform | Platform scope | Best-aligned environment | Operational trade-off | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Sangfor aSV | KVM-based hypervisor within Sangfor HCI and Cloud Platform; bundled networking, storage, and security | VMware estates evaluating an integrated alternative | Evaluation centers on the bundled Sangfor stack and migration tooling | 
| VMware | VMware Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, and advanced services | Established vSphere teams and integrations | Package selection and licensing changes affect total cost | 
| Nutanix | HCI platform with AHV, AOS storage, and Flow networking | Teams standardizing on an integrated hybrid-cloud platform | Existing servers must fit the certified hardware list | 
| Proxmox | Open-source KVM and container virtualization | Budget-focused teams comfortable managing infrastructure themselves | More manual storage, networking, HA, and recovery setup | 
| Red Hat | OpenShift Virtualization for VMs alongside containers | Container modernization and existing Ansible operations | Kubernetes-platform overhead for VM-focused teams | 
| Microsoft Hyper-V | Type-1 hypervisor included with Windows Server | Windows-heavy estates extending into Azure | Management and integration advantages favor the Microsoft stack | 
| Oracle | OCI infrastructure and Oracle application services | Oracle Database and Oracle-application-heavy estates | Less differentiated fit for mixed application portfolios | 
For a geographically focused comparison of private-cloud and HCI options, see VMware alternatives in Thailand.
Matching the Platform to Your Existing Estate
Your existing estate determines which platform advantages matter. Windows Server licensing favors Hyper-V, Oracle applications favor OCI, and container modernization favors OpenShift Virtualization. For a VMware migration, the deciding comparison includes bundled services and migration tooling alongside the skills and integrations your team would retain or replace.
The right choice among virtualization platforms for hybrid cloud environments depends almost entirely on starting conditions. VMware’s ecosystem depth remains unmatched, but licensing costs have changed the math significantly. Nutanix suits teams that want analyst-validated HCI at scale; Proxmox serves budget-focused shops comfortable with open-source assembly. Red Hat is the natural pick for container-modernization paths, Hyper-V makes sense inside committed Microsoft/Azure environments, and Oracle fits Oracle-application-heavy stacks. Teams migrating an existing VMware estate – particularly those evaluating cost-per-workload on a tight timeline – should also look hard at KVM-based alternatives that bundle networking and security into the base platform license. You’ll notice that bundling, more than any other single factor, is where the real cost differences tend to surface.
FAQ
Virtualization abstracts compute resources, while hybrid cloud connects on-premises and public-cloud environments through virtualization, containerization, and orchestration. For teams choosing among these seven platforms, the deciding factors are existing workloads, included services, and management fit. The hypervisor is one component of that deployment model, alongside the surrounding platform services.
What is virtualization in the cloud?
A hypervisor abstracts physical compute resources so multiple workloads can run as virtual machines. In hybrid environments, that abstraction supports workloads across on-premises servers and cloud platforms. Networking, storage, and management capabilities come from the surrounding platform stack.
What is a hybrid cloud deployment model?
It connects on-premises infrastructure with public-cloud resources. Virtualization abstracts compute, while containerization and cloud orchestration help workloads operate across the environments. Aerospike’s hybrid-cloud explanation describes how these technologies support interoperability.
What are the best virtualization platforms for hybrid cloud environments?
The seven options covered here are Sangfor aSV, VMware, Nutanix, Proxmox, Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Oracle. Selection depends on your estate: bundled HCI, established VMware integrations, open-source administration, container modernization, Microsoft/Azure alignment, or Oracle-heavy applications.
Checking the Hybrid Extension Before Platform Commitment
A VMware-based hybrid deployment needs an existing VMware foundation and a compatible cloud extension. For teams retaining vSphere, provider limitations belong in the platform comparison alongside licensing and included services. Pluralsight’s VMware hybrid-cloud guidance specifically calls for checking VMware documentation and the cloud provider’s limitations during selection.
Your current management tool does not disappear when the cloud extension arrives. Pluralsight’s guidance makes existing VMware use a condition of its VMware hybrid scenario, so a team managing another platform cannot assume the same design fits. Before committing, compare the proposed cloud provider’s documented limitations with the VMware deployment you actually run. That check belongs beside the license comparison, especially when retaining existing vSphere tooling is a major reason for staying with VMware.
articles.summary:
Enterprises are reevaluating their virtualization strategies following Broadcom’s VMware acquisition, with seven key platforms emerging as top contenders for managing modern hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure workloads.

### Key Points
- Sangfor aSV offers a KVM-based alternative that bundles networking, storage, and security to compete with VMware’s modular pricing.
- VMware remains the industry leader for ecosystem depth, though recent licensing changes have prompted many organizations to model total costs more aggressively.
- Nutanix provides a highly-rated, integrated hyper-converged infrastructure (HCI) platform that includes the AHV hypervisor at no additional license cost.
- Proxmox serves as a cost-effective, open-source option for teams comfortable with manual configuration and self-managed infrastructure.
- Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization is optimized for organizations prioritizing container modernization and Kubernetes-native workflows.
- Microsoft Hyper-V and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) offer specialized advantages for teams already heavily invested in Windows or Oracle-specific application stacks.

### Why it Matters
Selecting the right virtualization platform is a critical architectural decision that dictates long-term operational costs and technical flexibility. Choosing a platform that aligns with existing infrastructure and future modernization goals prevents costly rework and ensures seamless workload portability across hybrid environments.

articles.title: DraftKings gets four-month Louisiana license extension amid AI review
articles.author: ReadWrite
articles.content:
The Louisiana Gaming Control Board has unanimously granted DraftKings a conditional four-month license extension while it examines the company’s use of artificial intelligence in customer practices and delays a decision on full renewal. DraftKings can continue operating in the state under the interim arrangement.
The company’s existing Louisiana license expires November 10, 2026. The board has scheduled a renewal hearing for February 18, 2027, with a final decision expected afterward; the conditional extension is set to keep DraftKings authorized through February 19.
The Louisiana Gaming Control Board’s review follows a New York Times report alleging that DraftKings used AI to direct promotions and bonus inducements toward customers considered more likely to bet more. The reported practice was referred to internally as “elasticity.” The allegations are part of a broader regulatory examination of AI in sportsbook marketing.
There is also a separate ownership issue. The Louisiana State Police Gaming Enforcement Division found information indicating that some DraftKings shareholders with stakes of 5% or more had not completed customary suitability reviews. Assistant Attorney General Houston told the board the investigation was incomplete and that regulators needed additional time to examine the allegations and shareholder question.
The board has not found evidence that DraftKings violated a licensing or moral obligation. Its decision leaves both matters under review while the company operates under conditional authorization.
DraftKings disputes the reported AI use
DraftKings President of Operations and cofounder Paul Liberman appeared before the board to address the concerns. He denied that the company used AI in the manner described in the reporting or used the technology to harm consumers. Liberman also said DraftKings keeps records showing whether customers are winning or losing.
Legal Sports Report reported that the conditional renewal includes deadlines for DraftKings to provide shareholder suitability materials and written responses about AI use, prediction-market activity, digital offerings to Louisiana residents, and other regulatory questions. The company must also review and certify its marketing materials, commercials and digital ads for responsible-gambling compliance.
The conditions require a senior company representative to handle communications with the board within seven days. DraftKings must submit several materials within 30 days and provide monthly compliance reports covering areas such as new digital products, promotions, responsible-gambling systems, customer complaints and unresolved compliance issues.
Board Chairman Chris Hebert described the conditional approval as a way for regulators to complete their oversight and give DraftKings an opportunity to respond. The board’s action is not a finding that the company engaged in wrongdoing.
February hearing will set the next decision point
DraftKings will remain authorized to operate while state investigators continue their work and the company responds to the board’s conditions. The February 18 hearing is the next scheduled step toward a full license decision, with the extension running through the following day.
articles.summary:
The Louisiana Gaming Control Board has granted DraftKings a four-month conditional license extension while regulators investigate the company’s use of artificial intelligence and shareholder suitability requirements.

### Key Points
- The Louisiana Gaming Control Board issued a conditional license extension for DraftKings that remains effective through February 19, 2027.
- Regulators are investigating allegations that DraftKings used artificial intelligence to target promotions toward high-betting customers, a practice internally referred to as "elasticity."
- The board is reviewing whether shareholders with stakes of 5% or more have completed mandatory suitability reviews required by state law.
- DraftKings must submit monthly compliance reports and certify that all marketing materials and digital advertisements adhere to responsible-gambling standards.
- A formal renewal hearing is scheduled for February 18, 2027, to determine the company's long-term licensing status in Louisiana.

### Why it Matters
This regulatory scrutiny highlights the growing tension between sportsbook operators and state authorities regarding the ethical use of predictive algorithms in gambling. The outcome of this investigation could set a significant precedent for how AI-driven marketing practices are monitored and regulated across the broader U.S. sports betting industry.

articles.title: Google Home Speaker is downloading huge amounts of data, and users need it to stop
articles.author: nickodiaz@sbcglobal.net (Nickolas Diaz) , Nickolas Diaz
articles.content:
What you need to know
- Google Home Speaker users have noticed that the device has consumed an enormous amount of data in the background.
- The device was reportedly spotted consuming several terabytes of data in a single month without much use.
- Google is reportedly aware of the problem and has started rolling out a fix.
Users on social media are waking up to a startling truth: their Google Home Speaker has been incredibly active in the background. There's no clear reason why, but the amount of data is staggering.
Posts on the Google Home subreddit draw attention to an unfathomable amount of data being consumed by the Home Speaker (via 9to5Google). The user states that they've "got one old Google Mini and three of the new Google speakers." What's more, these devices aren't used for more than 20 minutes a day. This is strange, considering the user reports one of their Google Home Speakers consumed over 140GB of data in a day.
Combined, the user states their three speakers consumed 6TB of data "in under a month." Another user with a Home Speaker reported the same, stating, "Something’s up with them. This just started in the past 2 weeks for mine." This issue appears to be confined to the Google Home Speaker, as a user with a Nest Audio couldn't find an unusual amount of data consumption.
The publication speculated on this, too, but one Redditor said their speaker downloaded 20GB in a single day. However, they added that "It kept downloading firmware and failing to install it." This makes it seem like the device got caught in the worst possible loop of downloading and failing.
Google reportedly informed the publication that this is an issue with the Home Speaker. It adds that "a fix is already rolling out" to address this problem. Android Central has reached out to Google for more information, and we will update this post when we hear back.
Hungry, hungry speaker
I'd be concerned if I woke up one day and saw huge spikes of data being consumed by a Home Speaker. For what reason is it doing this, you know? It's a concerning issue, especially for something always connected to the internet (hence the data consumption). What makes it worse is if you don't use it that often, but maybe sparingly for queries here and there. The good thing is that Google is aware. Let's hope it doesn't happen again.
The Google Home Speaker is the company's new beginning for AI in the home. Gemini is integrated throughout the product to assist users with daily queries and more. While the device has gotten off without a hitch (for the most part), the Home Speaker did struggle this summer. Users reported incredibly slow response times from Gemini.
A latency problem was the culprit. Users reported that on the first day, there were no issues; however, after the second, "...every single question (even 'hello') needs at least 30s of answer time." Many queries that users would have for Gemini would time out, as the AI couldn't respond within a meaningful time. What's more, Google's smart home devices beyond the Home Speaker struggled, too.
Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android
Google had to roll out a software update to solve this issue, which is strange. Shortly before these issues appeared, the company rolled out a Gemini update for its smart home devices to make it "snappier." That seemingly backfired and required more tuning to get it right.
Nickolas is always excited about tech and getting his hands on it. Writing for him can vary from delivering the latest tech story to scribbling in his journal. When Nickolas isn't hitting a story, he's often grinding away at a game or chilling with a book in his hand.

articles.summary:
Google Home Speaker users are reporting massive, unexplained data consumption reaching several terabytes per month, prompting the company to begin rolling out a software fix for the issue.

### Key Points
- Users reported individual Google Home Speakers consuming up to 140GB of data in a single day.
- Total data usage across multiple devices reached 6TB in less than one month for some households.
- Reports suggest the issue may stem from a failed firmware update loop causing repeated, unsuccessful download attempts.
- Google has acknowledged the problem and confirmed that a software patch is currently being deployed to affected devices.
- The issue appears isolated to the Google Home Speaker, with other models like the Nest Audio remaining unaffected.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the potential for significant financial impact on users with data-capped internet plans when smart home devices malfunction. It also underscores the risks associated with background firmware updates, which can lead to excessive bandwidth consumption if software installation processes fail repeatedly.

articles.title: Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo
articles.author: Juli Clover
articles.content:
With just three days to go until the iPhone Duo is released, Apple is getting ready for the launch. Behind the scenes, the App Store now has screenshots of Apple's built-in apps running on the Duo. We've seen some apps in marketing materials, but images of the ones we haven't seen give us an idea of what it will be like using the iPhone Duo day to day.
Many apps are shown in landscape orientation with an iPad-like interface that uses some of the screen real estate for sidebar navigation. Other apps use the full screen for more viewing space.
Some apps have a dual view that goes beyond sidebar navigation. In Contacts, the app is divided into a list of names and a view for editing information.
The Siri app doesn't have a traditional sidebar, but it also doesn't get a full split. The left part of the interface is a tiled view of conversations, while the full conversation can be viewed on the right.
The iPhone Duo adopts a vertical dock and vertical navigation bars on the right side of the display in both open and closed views. The exception is an open view with the iPhone Duo held vertically, similar to an iPad in portrait orientation. When positioned that way, navigation bars remain at the bottom of the interface.
Apple's screenshots don't show many apps in the unfolded vertical orientation, but it is a viewing option. Apple says it's ideal for apps that use the keyboard or for browsing in Safari.
Apps like Preview have palettes at the bottom for selecting tools, and those are combined with sidebars, navigation bars, or both. Markup editing gives a good preview of what drawing and photo editing apps will be like, with a large amount of display space paired with a bottom tool palette.
Apps that don't need large navigation bars have widescreen views that take up the whole display. Apps that do have navigation bars have an option to tap to hide the bar.
Floating popovers show up when you press and hold on an icon. The popovers aren't scaled up and take up less room on the display than they do on Apple's smaller iPhones.
When you're on the Home Screen, you'll see the Today view on the left of the display with your widgets, while app icons are on the right. The status bar is in the upper-right corner, and the Lock Screen icons like Flashlight and Camera are in the bottom right. The inner display doesn't have an always-visible Dynamic Island because there is no Face ID and the FaceTime camera is under the screen. Apple is still using the Dynamic Island, which expands out from the side of the display for Live Activities and alerts. The outer display has a small vertical Dynamic Island that includes the camera cutout.
Most of the App Store screenshots have the iPhone Duo unfolded in landscape orientation, though some also show what apps will look like on the smaller outer display.
Apps will be able to transition quickly from open to closed and to different positions, and Apple made an effort to keep navigation buttons in the same place for a unified experience no matter how you're using it.
Open and closed aren't the only options for the iPhone Duo. Few screenshots show the positions, but the Duo can be used laptop-style at an angle for watching videos or standing in a tent shape with the outer display visible. You can also use it partially open and held like a book.
Screenshots also don't show two apps used side by side or multiple windows of the same app like Safari, both of which are options. We'll see a deluge of iPhone Duo updates for third-party apps when the device comes out.
The iPhone Duo is launching on October 23, which is this Friday. We should be getting media reviews and first impressions as soon as tomorrow since we'll be two days out from release.
(Thanks, Alireza!)
articles.summary:
Apple is preparing for the October 23 launch of the iPhone Duo by updating App Store screenshots to showcase how built-in applications adapt to the device's foldable display.

### Key Points
- The iPhone Duo features a versatile interface that supports landscape, portrait, and laptop-style orientations for various apps.
- Built-in apps like Contacts and Preview utilize sidebars, split-screen views, and bottom tool palettes to maximize the expanded screen real estate.
- The device includes a vertical dock and navigation bars that maintain consistent placement across different folding positions.
- The inner display hides the FaceTime camera under the screen, while the Dynamic Island expands from the side for alerts and Live Activities.
- Users can transition between open and closed states, with the device supporting multitasking features like side-by-side app usage.

### Why it Matters
This launch represents a significant shift in Apple's mobile hardware strategy by introducing a foldable form factor that requires a redesigned software interface. The success of the iPhone Duo will likely influence future app development standards and set a new benchmark for how iOS adapts to non-traditional screen sizes.

articles.title: Nikkei data breach affected over 1.8 million records
articles.author: Pierluigi Paganini
articles.content:
Japanese media company Nikkei has disclosed a data breach affecting more than 1.8 million records. The company, known for its financial news publications, including The Nikkei and the Financial Times, said attackers accessed a cloud service used for system development. On the morning of October 7, the hackers used previously stolen credentials to gain access. Nikkei has published details of the incident in an official statement.
“A cloud service used by Nikkei Inc. for system development was accessed without authorization, and as of October 16, approximately 1.83 million items of personal information had been leaked.” reads the data breach notice published by the company. “About 150,000 items contained one or more of the following: name, email address, postal address, phone number or date of birth. Of these, about 120,000 included an email address. About 1.68 million items contained only information that cannot identify an individual. No credit card information is included in any of the leaked information.”
The security breach did not compromise financial information.
The company reported the breach to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission on October 11. The company is still investigating the scope of the security breach and what personal information was stolen.
According to the notice, attackers used stolen login details to access a cloud service on October 7. Nikkei has since blocked the stolen credentials.
As of October 16, the company had found no signs of further damage, such as misuse of the leaked data, system outages, or changes to its data.
Nikkei apologized for the incident and said it would inform all individuals whose personal information was exposed.
In May 2022, the Japanese media giant Nikkei disclosed a ransomware attack, while in November 2025, it disclosed a data breach stemming from the compromise of a Slack account.

articles.summary:
Japanese media giant Nikkei confirmed a data breach involving 1.83 million records after unauthorized actors accessed a cloud development environment using stolen credentials on October 7.

### Key Points
- Attackers compromised a cloud service used for system development, exposing 1.83 million records.
- Approximately 150,000 records contained sensitive personal data, including names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, or birth dates.
- The remaining 1.68 million leaked items consist of non-identifiable information.
- Nikkei confirmed that no credit card details or financial information were compromised in the incident.
- The company reported the breach to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission on October 11.
- Nikkei has blocked the compromised credentials and is currently notifying all affected individuals.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the ongoing vulnerability of corporate cloud development environments to credential-based attacks. As Nikkei faces its third major security disclosure since 2022, the breach underscores the critical need for robust multi-factor authentication and stricter access controls to protect user data.

articles.title: Your car’s smartest features are opening doors for hackers
articles.author: Mike McRae
articles.content:
The biggest threat to your car was once a coat hanger combined with a questionable sense of morality. Today, thieves barely need to leave the comfort of their own couch.
Modern vehicles are computers on wheels, communicating with your smartphone, other cars, satellites, and cloud servers to navigate, entertain, and even drive for you. It's all so convenient, right up until somebody with less-than-honorable intentions finds a way into your vehicle’s digital conversation.
A new study by researchers at the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden has found that the biggest cybersecurity risks facing modern vehicles are now found less within the vehicle’s core operations and increasingly outside of the cars themselves. And some of the weaknesses are embarrassingly basic.
The researchers examined 413 software vulnerabilities affecting connected vehicles between January 2022 and September 2024, comparing their findings with security issues documented over the previous decade.
They discovered a striking change in where the problems are turning up.
Decades ago, car thieves needed to have physical access to a vehicle to steal it. Attack patterns have since evolved to become more remote. External applications – including websites, apps, and cloud services – now account for more than a third of identified weaknesses. That's nearly three times the proportion found in earlier research.
The consequences aren’t pretty. Vulnerabilities in software can result in attacks that compromise its entire ability to drive safely, meaning security is no longer just a matter of keeping your car safe. It’s about you staying alive.
In 2015, security researchers famously demonstrated how they could remotely interfere with a Jeep Cherokee's steering, brakes, and accelerator after gaining access through its infotainment system.
More than a decade later, weaknesses involving entertainment and communication systems remain a concern.
One documented vulnerability in a Škoda infotainment system, for example, could allow an attacker connected to the vehicle's Wi-Fi to crash the system under certain conditions.
Not quite a Hollywood-style highway hijacking, but hardly a feature you'd expect to find in the brochure.
While some more nefarious syndicates might hold your steering or brakes for ransom, a far more common target is your private information. Your address, your movements, your daily routine, and potentially even where you park when you're supposed to be at work.
The risks aren't entirely hypothetical. In December 2024, researchers revealed that location information associated with around 800,000 vehicles from Volkswagen Group brands had been left accessible online.
Attackers exploited unsecured Amazon Web Services credentials used by a third-party vendor to collect precise GPS locations and personal details, potentially allowing someone to reconstruct a driver's movements.
Fortunately, the exposure was addressed before any known malicious exploitation. Yet our privacy is only part of the problem. The study also found a worrying shift in the severity of reported vulnerabilities. Nearly 45% were classified as high severity, with another 16% listed as critical. By comparison, an earlier study found just 5% of vulnerabilities fell into the critical category.
That doesn't mean hackers are now commandeering cars by the millions. A vulnerability is a potential opportunity, not evidence that somebody has successfully exploited it.
The researchers identified problems lurking in third-party software libraries used by automotive developers, highlighting how security flaws can find their way into vehicles long before they leave the factory. The findings point to a simple lesson for manufacturers: security needs to be built into every stage of development, not bolted on as an afterthought.
Keeping entertainment systems isolated from safety-critical controls would also help ensure a compromised playlist doesn't become a compromised vehicle.
For drivers, the advice is familiar: install software updates, use strong passwords, and think carefully about the personal information shared with connected services.
After all, your car already knows where you've been. There's no reason to let everyone else know, too.
This research was published in Software Quality Journal
Source: TechXplore
articles.summary:
Researchers from the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers University of Technology report that modern connected vehicles face increasing cybersecurity threats from external software, cloud services, and third-party applications.

### Key Points
- Researchers analyzed 413 software vulnerabilities in connected vehicles identified between January 2022 and September 2024.
- External applications, including websites and cloud services, now account for over one-third of all identified automotive security weaknesses.
- Approximately 61% of documented vulnerabilities are classified as high or critical severity, a significant increase from historical data.
- A December 2024 incident exposed the GPS locations and personal data of 800,000 Volkswagen Group vehicles due to unsecured third-party cloud credentials.
- Security flaws often originate in third-party software libraries integrated into vehicles during the manufacturing process.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward remote, software-based vulnerabilities transforms vehicle security from a simple theft-prevention issue into a critical matter of driver safety and personal privacy. As cars become increasingly connected, manufacturers must prioritize cybersecurity throughout the entire development lifecycle to prevent potential exploitation of safety-critical systems.

articles.title: Baseus Security U2 Pro Launches With Dual 3K Cameras and a Spotlight That Tracks Intruders
articles.author: Scott Webster
articles.content:
Baseus has introduced the Security PrimeSentinel U2 Pro, an outdoor security camera system that takes a more active approach to home protection. Featuring dual 3K cameras, 360-degree tracking, and a motorized spotlight that follows moving subjects, the U2 Pro aims to do more than capture footage of suspicious activity.
The Baseus Security U2 Pro launches in the US on October 20, 2026, with a suggested retail price of $279.99. It’s designed for homeowners looking to monitor driveways, entrances, and backyards without relying entirely on traditional motion-activated floodlights.
Two Cameras Keep Watch From Different Angles
The U2 Pro combines a fixed 3K camera with a second 3K pan-and-tilt camera capable of tracking movement across 360 degrees. The fixed camera monitors a designated area while the motorized camera follows people or vehicles moving around the property.
Both cameras feature a 130-degree field of view, 8x digital zoom, and night vision capabilities. This arrangement allows homeowners to maintain coverage of an entrance while simultaneously tracking activity elsewhere.
The system’s most unusual feature is its Target-Focused Deterrence Spotlight, which Baseus describes as an industry first. Rather than illuminating an entire area, the spotlight directs a concentrated beam toward a moving subject and follows their movements.
According to Baseus’ internal testing, the spotlight successfully tracked walking and jogging subjects at distances between 3 and 8 meters. It also tracked sprinting individuals at distances of 5 meters or greater. Real-world performance will depend on conditions and installation.
AI Alerts, Local Storage, and Solar Charging
Dual PIR motion sensors work with AI recognition to identify people, vehicles, and pets. The U2 Pro can generate contextual notifications describing detected activity, potentially reducing the need to review every recording.
Footage can be stored locally with support for up to 512GB of storage and AES/RSA encryption. Two-way audio, Alexa and Google Home compatibility, and remote access through the Baseus Security app round out its connected features.
A 7,800mAh rechargeable battery provides up to 150 days of operation without solar assistance, according to Baseus. The included 3W solar panel can reportedly supply enough energy for a day’s use with 40 minutes of sunlight under laboratory conditions.
The camera carries an IP65 weather-resistance rating and supports operating temperatures from -4°F to 122°F.
Pricing and Availability
The Baseus Security U2 Pro launches in the United States on October 20, priced at $279.99 MSRP. The company lists European pricing at €269.99, with a November 17 launch date.
For homeowners interested in a camera that can actively illuminate moving subjects, the U2 Pro offers an interesting alternative to conventional security cameras. Its tracking spotlight is the main attraction, though independent testing will be needed to establish how consistently it performs outside controlled conditions.

articles.title: Bitcoin price spikes to $83.3K as US stocks rise on Q3 earnings, oil falls
articles.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
articles.content:
Bitcoin price spikes to $83.3K as US stocks rise on Q3 earnings, oil falls
High US corporate earnings reports boosted stock markets and saw BTC price hit $83,300 before reversing at a 21-day trend line.
Bitcoin (BTC) returned to $83,000 after Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks gained on strong earnings reports.
Key points:
- Bitcoin gained up to 1.5%, joining upside in US stocks on the back of some higher-than-expected Q3 earnings results.
- Oil prices hit $101 per barrel early on Tuesday before dropping nearly 5% in hours as equities gained.
- BTC price action sought to challenge the 21-day simple moving average (SMA) at $83,230.
BTC price swings as US earnings, oil moves drive markets
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD gaining 1.5% to reach its highest levels since Oct. 14 before dropping back toward $82,000.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Crypto joined US stock markets in rallying as Q3 earnings reports beat expectations. Both General Motors and industrial conglomerate 3M beat earnings expectations, while the latter also increased its profit forecast.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.2% on the back of the results to hit levels last seen on Sept. 14. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index traded up 0.6% and 0.5% at the time of writing.
Dow Jones Industrial Average one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

CFDs on WTI crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
