“Improving moods regarding the prospects of modern technology have Wall Street breathing a sigh of relief as participants drop hedges, after the cost of volatility protection soared intraday on Friday, ahead of the intensifying selloff,” he wrote.
SpaceX is due to report Q3 performance figures after the market close on Tuesday, with Tesla and Meta due on Wednesday.
Bitcoin rejected at 21-day moving average
Bitcoin broke through a nearby wall of ask liquidity with its trip to $83,000, data from CoinGlass showed. Crypto markets saw $125 million in short liquidations between 10 a.m. and 11 a.m. ET.
Related: XRP 30-day exchange inflows pass 6B tokens as whales move to the sidelines

Bitcoin reached a high of $83,300 as cryptocurrency markets rallied alongside US stocks, which were bolstered by strong third-quarter earnings reports from major corporations like General Motors.

The simultaneous rally in equities and digital assets suggests that investor sentiment is stabilizing following recent tech-sector sell-offs. articles.title: iPhone Duo Is Delightful, and Different
articles.author: Josh Rubin
articles.content:
After a week with iPhone Duo, I’m pleased that Apple‘s first foldable can work as both a pocketable phone and a small tablet without compromising either. The 5.4-inch outer screen handles glances and quick maneuvers on the move and the 7.6-inch inner display opens for anything that deserves focus—a rhythm that has changed how and where I use a phone. The battery outlasts expectations and the hinge feels precise in its resistance, considered in its form and deeply satisfying to close. Years of iPhone muscle memory took a few days to yield, and some trade-offs, from the return to Touch ID to an incompatible MagSafe wallet, temper the delight without undoing it. Personally, the Duo also closes a loop that opened in 1999.
That year, my graduate thesis at ITP, NYU’s Interactive Telecommunications Program, was the conceptual design and interface prototyping of a future looking four-screen folding phone that Kent Hollrah and I called The Stack. It studied form setting function, with one configuration for reading, another for calls and another for maps, as much as it explored how software should behave on hardware that changes shape. Kent and I got a lot wrong in our forecast and a few things right, and it’s gratifying to see questions we once sketched answered, with far more finesse, in how the Duo’s postures shape its uses. I’ve tested many foldables over the years since they first came to market, but as someone embedded in the Apple ecosystem, this is the first I’ve been able to truly bring into daily life. It has also pared down what I carry. Until now I often traveled with an iPhone Pro alongside an iPad mini, the Duo now covers both. That hardly makes it an iPad killer, since there are still many tasks for which an iPad, especially one of the larger models, remains the best device.
The most surprising usage change is behavioral. Closed, the Duo is ideal for pruning an inbox with a thumb and firing off a terse response or, better, dictating one to Siri. When managing email requires more attention, opening the phone puts a message and the inbox side by side. That division of labor has spread beyond Mail. The outer screen is small enough to discourage lingering, so on the street I check, answer and pocket, saving the inner display for whenever I’m still, whether at a desk, on a sofa, at a café table or simply standing in place. The result is screen time with greater intentionality, and I feel more in control of when I let myself get pulled into a deep scroll. The open screen serves more than consumption, obviously. Making things, from photographing and editing images to writing, is far better on the larger canvas, and so is a round of Crossplay. The Stack argued that a device’s shape could direct its purpose, and it’s rewarding to watch that idea work as a behavioral nudge.
The initial delight of opening the Duo has settled into a quiet confidence, and its hinge now sets the bar for how every hinge should feel. Built from more than 100 components, it moves through its arc with measured tension, closer to a well-made notebook than a mechanism. Both displays share a 1.4:1 aspect ratio, so content scales up mid-task or reflows into a new layout if appropriate, and that continuity is the Duo’s most consequential design choice precisely because it goes unnoticed. A micro-blasted, 3D-printed titanium hinge cover contrasts with the mirror-polished Grade 5 titanium frame, making the spine read as a deliberate architectural element. Closed, it has the proportions of a passport and pockets as easily.
Foldability invites postures a slab phone can’t hold. Bent like a laptop, the Duo becomes a natural setup for watching videos of for FaceTime, its camera hidden beneath the inner display until needed, and a handy stand for shooting photos.
StandBy, which turns a docked iPhone into an ambient clock and widget display, no longer needs a charger on the Duo, and I’ve used it in every configuration. Fully open on a charger at my desk, it becomes nearly a home dashboard, pairing two small widgets and a large one on the left with an extra-large widget on the right. Partially folded and stood like a book, the inner display does the same without a cable. Tented into an inverted V, the outer screen offers clock, photo, modular, weather and calendar faces, and a Wake Up alarm in that position brings a glow that slowly brightens across the inner display.
Laid open and flat on a table, the Duo rocks on its camera plateau, a problem Apple’s Folio with Kickstand, designed for upright, angled viewing, doesn’t solve. Somebody will likely design an accessory that levels it. In the meantime, I’ve been sliding my phone tatami mat under the upper half, which tilts the screen to a pleasant angle and ends the wobble.
Sound remains consistent regardless of form. Because the distance between the speakers changes as the Duo opens, folds and rotates, Apple compensates with real-time tuning, and whether the phone is tented, propped or held open, audio never lurches with a change of position. Apple says the microphones are likewise placed for each configuration, though I haven’t heard a Duo call from the other end.
Two screens haven’t taken a toll on battery. A cell in each half, with power managed by custom silicon, behaves as a single battery, and Apple claims up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display versus 31 on the inner. On a full day running around the city, I carried a charger out of habit and never needed it, a genuine shift for someone used to topping up daily. A breakdown in Settings showing drain by display or folded state (this is a feature request) would make the trade-off between modes legible rather than intuited.
Moving from a conventional iPhone is where the Duo demands extra attention. The software looks as familiar as ever, but on the Duo, controls that have long lived along the top and bottom of the screen migrate to the side, so several interactions require relearning. Dynamic Island, the pill-shaped home for live alerts around the front camera, sits in a vertical rail along the right edge and pushes interface elements down, so in apps like Messages the back button doesn’t always land in the same place. Control Center screens are shorter, and after migration the last two rows of my layout spilled onto a new page. Neither issue is serious, and the adjustment has largely passed, though I still occasionally pause to recall where something lives. The clearest sign came when I picked up my 18 Pro after days of deliberately avoiding it, and the conventional phone was the one that felt foreign, and strikingly tall.
Authentication takes recalibration too. The Duo trades Face ID for Touch ID in the side button, so the first step is enrolling several fingers. I registered both index fingers and my right thumb, because the screen reorients to however the phone is held and the button lands somewhere different each time I seem to need it. Unlocking with Apple Watch shortens the path, with one quirk: holding the phone while it’s inside a pocket can unlock the phone, and more than once a tap on my wrist was the first sign the Duo had woken and was pocket-dial-ready. Apple Pay is slower, since double-clicking and confirming with a fingerprint can’t match Face ID’s glance at a checkout counter. MagSafe wallets won’t attach because of the Duo’s size and shape, which stings for anyone who consolidated cards onto the back of their phone—I’ve had to get used to carrying a separate wallet again. I also miss the Action Button, which I had mapped to Gemini for quick lookups; Gemini answers those faster than Siri, whose handoff to an outside chatbot is limited to ChatGPT.
Two displays, four cameras and a hinge that holds whatever angle it’s given open up shooting scenarios a slab phone can’t. Unfolded, the outer screen faces the subject. Duo Preview shows people a live view of themselves while framing them with the rear cameras, so they can adjust their pose without waiting for direction. Kid Cue plays Snoopy animations there to draw a child’s gaze to the lens; turns out it makes adults smile too. Turned around, the same arrangement makes selfies with the 48MP rear cameras practical, framed on the outer screen rather than guessed at, provided you look at the lenses rather than the preview once the shot is framed, or your sightline drifts. Propped on a table, the Duo becomes its own photographer: Smart Take uses on-device models to release the shutter once everyone is posed, retiring the sprint back from a self-timer. Dual Capture records the front and rear cameras at once, and Duo FaceTime lets someone beside you join a video call through the outer display and camera, so nobody has to crowd around one screen.
The Duo’s camera system isn’t the 18 Pro’s equal. Both models share the 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, Cinematic focus effects applied after capture and the new texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles are a joy to find here. The Duo’s 48MP Fusion main camera can default to 26, 28 or 35 mm and reaches 2x the same way the 18 Pro does, but without the Pro’s dedicated telephoto, the 4x and 8x options are missing. The mechanical variable aperture and manual Pro controls are exclusive to the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.
That gap is where iPhone Handoff earns its place. The iOS 27 feature moves one phone number to whichever of two iPhones is unlocked, and with T-Mobile it has carried mine between the Duo and the 18 Pro seamlessly. The Duo handles daily life, from reading and writing to triage and calls to casual photography, while the 18 Pro stays at the ready for situations that call for more camera control. The two meet in iCloud Photos, where shots from the Pro arrive on the Duo, which has power to spare for editing and, unfolded, makes a finer darkroom than any slab.
iPhone Duo arrives 23 October 2026 at $1,999 for the 256GB configuration, in Night Sky and Star White. It asks its owner to unlearn a few habits and accept a few compromises, and repays both with a phone that stays small when life is in motion, opens into a canvas when it isn’t and, for anyone who has imagined such a device for decades, offers the pleasure of finally carrying one.
articles.summary:
The new Apple iPhone Duo, a foldable device featuring a 5.4-inch outer screen and 7.6-inch inner display, launches on October 23, 2026, with a starting price of $1,999.

### Key Points
- The device features a precision-engineered titanium hinge and dual-display architecture designed for seamless content scaling.
- It replaces Face ID with side-button Touch ID and requires users to adapt to new interface layouts and navigation controls.
- Camera capabilities include Duo Preview and Smart Take, though it lacks the dedicated telephoto lens found on the iPhone 18 Pro.
- Battery life is managed by custom silicon across two internal cells, supporting extended use without requiring mid-day charging.
- The phone is available in Night Sky and Star White colorways, starting at a 256GB storage capacity.

### Why it Matters
The iPhone Duo represents Apple’s first entry into the foldable market, signaling a shift in how the company balances hardware form factors with user behavior. By offering a device that functions as both a compact phone and a tablet, Apple is challenging the dominance of traditional slab-style smartphones while testing consumer willingness to accept specific trade-offs in exchange for increased screen versatility.

articles.title: Germany’s most popular party targeted by unknown hackers
articles.author: RT
articles.content:
Hackers target Germany’s most popular party
Germany’s most popular party, Alternative for Germany (AfD), has suffered a massive cyberattack, with unknown hackers reportedly stealing and publishing hundreds of thousands of internal emails, while the country’s political establishment seeks grounds to outlaw the opposition party.
The breach, which was first reported by Bild on Tuesday, reportedly exposed 421,179 emails totaling 281 gigabytes, including correspondence involving AfD co-chair Alice Weidel, honorary chairman Alexander Gauland, and other senior party figures.
The leaked material reportedly includes photographs of identity documents, bank statements, invoices, membership applications, and internal party lists. Bild said it examined a small sample of the files, including an identity card belonging to Markus Frohnmaier, the deputy leader of the AfD parliamentary group in the Bundestag.
The identities and motives of the hackers are unknown, and the authenticity of the published material has not been independently established.
The AfD confirmed that a hosting provider working with the party was hacked in September, but disputed suggestions that its current communications systems was compromised.
“Only a few email inboxes were unlawfully copied, most of which had not been used for years,” a party spokesman told Bild, adding that current federal party email accounts were unaffected.
The AfD condemned the breach as an “attack on the German party system and therefore on democracy” and said it reported the cyberattack to the security authorities.
No statement from investigators or condemnation of the breach by senior government officials has emerged as of early Wednesday.
The leaked correspondence has already drawn scrutiny from activists seeking to outlaw the party. Valentina Chiofalo, a representative of the German civil liberties organization Gesellschaft fuer Freiheitsrechte, told taz that the stolen emails could help strengthen the case for banning the AfD, while their publication and journalistic scrutiny could also shape public opinion against the party.
The attack comes amid an escalating campaign by Germany’s established political parties to isolate and potentially ban the AfD. The Euroskeptic party, which advocates stricter immigration controls and opposes Berlin’s military support for Ukraine and sanctions on Russia, has surged to 30% support in the latest INSA poll for Bild, opening a 12-point lead over Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU/CSU bloc, which has slumped to 18%.
Earlier this month, the AfD secured the presidency of Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament for the first time, breaking through the political ‘firewall’ maintained by establishment parties. Its rise prompted Social Democratic parliamentary leaders to demand the creation of a federal-state working group to examine a possible ban, accusing the AfD of threatening democracy from within and promoting extremism.
Germany’s domestic intelligence agency has also sought to classify the party as a confirmed right-wing extremist organization, but a Cologne court blocked the designation in February pending further legal proceedings.
The AfD has rejected the accusations, portraying the proposed ban as an attempt to overturn the will of millions of voters and eliminate political competition.
articles.summary:
Unknown hackers have leaked over 420,000 internal emails from Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, exposing sensitive personal documents and private correspondence of senior party leadership figures.

### Key Points
- The breach involved 281 gigabytes of data, including bank statements, identity documents, and invoices belonging to officials like Alice Weidel and Alexander Gauland.
- The AfD confirmed a third-party hosting provider was compromised in September but claimed current federal email systems remain secure.
- The leaked files include an identity card belonging to Bundestag deputy leader Markus Frohnmaier, according to reports from the newspaper Bild.
- The AfD currently leads national polling with 30% support, significantly outpacing the CDU/CSU bloc despite ongoing efforts by political rivals to pursue a formal party ban.
- German authorities and intelligence agencies have previously investigated the party for alleged extremism, though a court blocked a formal designation earlier this year.

### Why it Matters
The leak provides potential evidence for activists and political opponents currently campaigning to outlaw the AfD on grounds of extremism. This incident intensifies the volatile political climate in Germany as the party continues to gain electoral momentum despite efforts by the establishment to isolate it.

articles.title: Why Were Trump Officials Trying to Hack Into a Voting Machine?
articles.author: Ellie Quinlan Houghtaling
articles.content:
President Donald Trump has made supposed voting integrity a fundamental component of his brand since the 2020 presidential election. So why did his administration try to hack a voting machine?
Insiders that spoke to ProPublica shared that political appointees at the Department of Homeland Security had asked the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, or CISA, to covertly obtain a voting machine, break into it, and report back to the White House.
The directive reportedly shocked CISA employees, who felt the request was antithetical to their mission of thwarting potential hackers. Furthermore, staff were concerned by another DHS request that would have restricted CISA from notifying the voting machine companies of their findings.
“My thought was they could keep it in their back pocket to invalidate any results they don’t like,” one former official told ProPublica. “This goes against everything CISA represents.”
The request was ultimately not fulfilled, in no small part because the agents capable of pulling off such an operation were terminated by Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency. Eventually the political appointees stopped pressing the issue, according to ProPublica.
Over the course of Trump’s second administration, more than 1,000 employees have been pushed out of CISA—about a third of the agency. But CISA could be on the brink of more devastating cuts: The president’s 2027 budget proposal would shrink funding for the agency by $700 million, a number that could result in another 900 employees getting axed.
Against all democratic principles, Trump has repeatedly attacked the concept of voting and stoked election conspiracies for his own personal gain. He has continually made unfounded claims about voter fraud, pressured state election officials, strong-armed state legislatures to reshape their districts for the benefit of his agenda, and attempted to dismantle mail-in voting—all to remain in power and disregard or overthrow electoral results that he has perceived as less than favorable.
articles.summary:
Former Trump administration officials reportedly pressured the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to covertly hack voting machines to potentially invalidate unfavorable election results during his second term.

### Key Points
- Political appointees at the Department of Homeland Security directed CISA staff to obtain and breach voting machines without notifying the manufacturers.
- CISA employees resisted the directive, viewing the request as a violation of the agency’s core mission to protect election infrastructure from cyber threats.
- The operation was never executed, partly due to the termination of key personnel by the Department of Government Efficiency.
- Over 1,000 CISA employees have been removed during the current administration, representing approximately one-third of the agency's total workforce.
- The president’s 2027 budget proposal seeks a $700 million funding reduction for CISA, which could lead to the loss of 900 additional staff positions.

### Why it Matters
These reports highlight a significant tension between political leadership and the nonpartisan agencies tasked with maintaining the integrity of national election systems. If federal resources are used to undermine rather than protect voting infrastructure, it could permanently erode public trust in democratic processes and institutional oversight.

articles.title: Benchmarking Bot Detection Systems Against Modern AI Agents in 2026
articles.author: Milena Rmus, Mayank Agrawal, Mathew Hardy
articles.content:
We revisit our bot detection benchmark with stealth browsers and modern AI agents, and find detection rates ranging from 9% to 99%.
A year ago, we evaluated five leading bot detection systems (Proof of Human, Google reCAPTCHA v3, hCaptcha, Fingerprint Pro, and Cloudflare Turnstile) against automated browsers programmed to complete a set of predefined tasks. Detection rates varied substantially, ranging from 33% to 87%. Systems that incorporated behavioral signals alongside device-level signals generally outperformed those relying on device information alone.
Since then, browser automation has advanced considerably. Modern AI agents can interpret webpages, plan actions, and interact with interfaces through increasingly capable browser environments. We therefore revisited our benchmark with an expanded set of adversaries, including conventional browser automation, stealth browsers, and AI-powered browsing agents, and tested a similar set of detection systems: Proof of Human, Google reCAPTCHA v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, and Cloudflare Bot Management. The results reveal similarly wide variation in detection performance.
In this post, we examine how each system performed, where it failed, and what these results suggest about the challenges of distinguishing humans from increasingly capable AI agents.
Our task used a five-question survey combining multiple-choice items with open-ended responses. Each of the five adversaries (i.e., AI agents) attempted the survey 20 times, yielding up to 100 sessions per detection system. Some detection systems failed or crashed before session completion, leaving between 89 and 100 evaluable sessions for each system.
The table below summarizes the detection systems included in the benchmark and the signals each uses to identify automated activity.
| Detection system | Description | 
|---|---|
| Proof of Human | Uses a machine-learning model to classify sessions as human or automated based on both behavioral and device signals, including typing, mouse movements, clicks, and scrolling. | 
| Google reCAPTCHA v3 | Assigns each session a score from 0 to 1 indicating the likelihood that the user is human. It operates without a visible challenge and considers browser-integrity and Google-side reputation signals; the site determines the threshold for accepting a session. | 
| hCaptcha | Presents an “I am human” checkbox and evaluates the browser's risk profile. Depending on the result, it either verifies the session immediately or presents an image-based challenge that must be completed. | 
| Cloudflare Turnstile | Performs browser-integrity checks in the background and issues a verification token when a session passes. It generally operates without a puzzle but may request user interaction when signals are ambiguous. | 
| Cloudflare Bot Management | Evaluates requests using heuristics and machine-learning models trained on traffic across             Cloudflare's network. Although the full system assigns scores from 1 (automated) to 99 (human), the             Pro-tier implementation returns broader classifications such as likely_human, likely_automated, automated, or verified_bot. | 
Our set of adversaries covers increasingly sophisticated forms of automation: conventional scripted browsers, stealth browsers designed to conceal automation signals, and AI agents capable of navigating webpages and completing tasks autonomously.
| Adversary | Description | 
|---|---|
| Chromium | A standard Chromium browser automated through Playwright and the Chrome DevTools Protocol, without             stealth modifications. It retains common indicators of automation, such as navigator.webdriver and CDP-related artifacts, and serves as the baseline “obvious             bot.” | 
| CloakBrowser | A stealth-focused Chromium fork that modifies browser fingerprints, including GPU, canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, user-agent, and TLS signals, at the source-code level. We ran it through a residential proxy with its optional humanization features for mouse and keyboard input enabled. | 
| Browser Use | An open-source AI-agent framework that uses an LLM (Claude Opus in our setup) and visual page information to plan actions and operate an unmodified browser from cloud infrastructure. | 
| Perplexity Comet | UsesPerplexity's AI-powered browser, which uses an LLM and visual information to navigate webpages and complete tasks. | 
| Grok | xAI's browser-use agent, which uses an LLM and visual information to navigate and complete web tasks. | 
We found that detection performance varied substantially across systems. Aggregated across all adversaries, Proof of Human identified 99% of automated sessions, followed by reCAPTCHA v3 at 69.4%, hCaptcha at 44.3%, Cloudflare Turnstile at 42.1%, and Cloudflare Bot Management at 9.1%.
Performance differed considerably by adversary. The clearest split was between scripted browsers and AI agents. hCaptcha and Cloudflare Turnstile caught nearly every scripted Chromium and CloakBrowser session but few of the AI-agent sessions. reCAPTCHA v3 showed the opposite pattern, identifying most agent sessions but none from CloakBrowser. Cloudflare Bot Management caught few sessions from any adversary, while Proof of Human detected at least 95% of sessions overall.
As most detection systems are black-box, we cannot directly determine which signals produced each result. However, the systems' observed behavior, together with publicly available documentation, suggests several likely sources for this failure:
Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these results:
Our results suggest that bot detection is entering a new phase. Traditional automation signals remain effective against scripted browsers, but they are less reliable against AI agents that genuine browser environments intelligently. Interactive challenges may offer limited protection when vision-capable agents can interpret and complete them. And as browser-level indicators become easier to avoid, the way a user behaves throughout a session becomes increasingly important for distinguishing human activity from automation.
Future benchmarks should test larger volumes of traffic, include human participants to measure false-positive rates, and evaluate more complex tasks and emerging agents. At Proof of Human, we will continue tracking these changes and developing methods in this evolving threat landscape. To test Proof of Human on your own application, visit poh.org.
Milena Rmus, Mayank Agrawal, and Mathew Hardy work at Proof of Human, PBC, where they are building Proof of Human, an invisible authentication system for the web. Previously, they completed PhDs in cognitive science at the University of California, Berkeley (Milena) and Princeton University (Mayank and Matt).
articles.summary:
A new benchmark study reveals that modern bot detection systems show highly inconsistent performance, with success rates ranging from 9% to 99% against advanced AI-powered browsing agents.

### Key Points
- Researchers tested five detection systems: Proof of Human, Google reCAPTCHA v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, and Cloudflare Bot Management.
- Adversaries included standard Chromium scripts, stealth-focused browsers like CloakBrowser, and AI agents such as Perplexity Comet, Grok, and Browser Use.
- Proof of Human achieved the highest detection rate at 99%, while Cloudflare Bot Management identified only 9.1% of automated sessions.
- Detection systems struggled to distinguish between traditional scripted bots and newer AI agents that can interpret visual webpage data to complete tasks.
- Performance varied significantly by tool, with some systems effectively blocking scripted browsers while failing to identify sophisticated AI-driven navigation.

### Why it Matters
The wide disparity in detection capabilities highlights a growing vulnerability as AI agents become increasingly adept at mimicking human behavior and bypassing traditional security signals. Businesses must recognize that legacy browser-integrity checks are becoming less reliable, necessitating a shift toward behavioral analysis to secure web applications against autonomous threats.

articles.title: AI for Teachers and Gemini Notebook (Formerly NotebookLM)
articles.author: coolcatteacher@gmail.com (Victoria A Davis, Cool Cat Teacher), Victoria A Davis, Cool Cat Teacher
articles.content:
I asked Gemini Notebook (formerly known as NotebookLM) a dress-code question, and it gave me the answer and the page number from our handbook. This is one of many efficiency ideas shared in today’s show.

School leaders and educators are increasingly using Gemini Notebook to streamline administrative tasks, such as querying policy handbooks and summarizing meetings, to prioritize meaningful human interactions over paperwork.

### Key Points
- Gemini Notebook, formerly known as NotebookLM, allows users to upload school handbooks and policy manuals to receive specific, cited answers to administrative questions.
- Author Vickie Echols, who wrote *AI for School Leaders*, advocates for using AI to reduce tedious workloads and prevent educator burnout.
- Superintendents are utilizing the tool to generate summaries and audio overviews of board meetings for stakeholders.
- Experts advise users to verify all AI-generated content for accuracy and to strictly avoid uploading confidential student information.
- Educators are also using generative AI tools like ChatGPT to refine email tone and improve professional communication.

### Why it Matters
Integrating AI into school administration helps leaders reclaim time previously lost to repetitive tasks, allowing them to focus on student engagement and staff support. By adopting these tools responsibly, educators can improve operational efficiency while maintaining the personal connections essential to a healthy school climate.
